description:
Round 2 of the white window. Round 1 pinned the develop texture's
filter NEAREST (the linear-filter class) and was WRONG: the owner
retracted it after a second clip still painted white. The pin stays
(it is not reverted), but the class is undecidable without eyes on
the window surface itself.

The evidence that forces a probe, not a fix:
- aspect-dependent: the WIDE clips (3840x2160 16:9, 4096x2560 16:10;
  surfaces 1080x607/675) paint white; the 4:3 clips (4096x3072,
  4080x3072; surfaces 1080x810/813) are healthy.
- zoom-proof: pinch-zoom brings nothing — the compositor's buffer is
  white at composition level, not mis-rect'd.
- stats-healthy: the SAME develop texture's stats pack shows real
  content, and the window draw+swap reports success.

So no host-side test can see it, and the two candidate classes
(draw-white vs surface-white) need the window surface's own pixel.
